subject: Hosted API sudden p95/p99 regressions — warmup/cold-start impact and customer escalations
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@finware.com>
To: evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, FinWare Platform Team <platform@finware.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 07:22:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted API: sharp p95/p99 spike this morning — urgent

Evelyn,

We're seeing a sharp degradation in tail latencies starting ~06:45 PT this morning. p95 jumped from ~220ms to ~1.2s and p99 is spiking above 2s. Concurrently the error rate (5xx) increased from ~0.1% to ~1.9%. This is directly impacting our real-time credit decisioning — we had to divert to a degraded mode.

Our SRE pulled traces and we see many cold-start-like events (long first-token times) on requests that map to our usual traffic fingerprint. Can you confirm if anything changed on your side (model swaps, routing, autoscale config)? We need ETA on mitigation and whether this will reoccur during peak tomorrow.

Attaching sample traces and a CSV of p95/p99 per minute.

Thanks,
Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Platform, FinWare
[Attachment: p95_metrics_20261201.csv]
From: evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@finware.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 07:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API: sharp p95/p99 spike this morning — urgent

Liam — thank you for the flag and the traces. I'm escalating immediately.

Top-level summary as I triage with the on-call team: we saw an autoscaler event that spun new GPU pods for the hosted pool around 06:30 PT; some of the newly provisioned pods experienced prolonged initialization (image pull + runtime warmup) which pushed first-token times up. We're treating this as a cold-start/warmup regression tied to autoscale bursts.

I'll get a concrete root cause and short-term mitigations within the hour. Marissa, loop me in on customer impact details and any compensation expectations we should prepare for. Rishi and Hannah, please confirm logs, image-pull latencies, and whether a config rollback or temporary pre-warm is possible.

—Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 08:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API: sharp p95/p99 spike this morning — urgent

Quick ops notes from initial triage and logs (attaching full debug dump). Observations:
- Autoscaler triggered ~24 pods for the hosted-gpu-2 pool between 06:28–06:36 PT due to a sudden burst in concurrent short-lived sessions.
- Median image pull time for affected nodes: 72s (registry eu-west was transiently slower).
- Runtime JIT / kernel registration on some CUDA kernels added ~200–400ms for first tokens on top of pull time.
- KV cache misses on these new pods caused additional model-init overhead in ~30% of requests.
- No model version changes were rolled during the window; routing policy and fallback were unchanged.

Short-term mitigations we can apply immediately:
1) Force-prewarm: provision a small pre-warmed replica set in us-west-2 for the next 12 hours to absorb spikes.
2) Adjust autoscaler thresholds: increase target CPU/RAM scale-up threshold to avoid many small simultaneous launches.
3) Serve fallback to an already-warmed smaller-quantized model for tail traffic for 2 hours.

I'll push the pre-warm and threshold patch now; will report back when done.

[Attachment: debug-log-20261201.txt]
—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@finware.com>, evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API: sharp p95/p99 spike this morning — urgent

Liam — I'm really sorry about the hit this morning. We're treating this as priority and will keep you updated each hour.

Action items we've started:
- Ops is pre-warming an additional 6 GPUs in your primary region (targeted at your traffic footprint).
- We're enabling a warmed fallback model for non-critical requests; this avoids full-init on spike traffic.
- We will provide a consolidated incident timeline and per-minute p95/p99 CSV once the mitigation is stabilized.

For transparency: if you prefer, we can schedule a brief 15-minute postmortem with your team and our SREs in the afternoon once we've stabilized. Would 2:30 PM PT work?

Marissa Cole
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Liam O'Connor <liam@finware.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 10:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API: sharp p95/p99 spike this morning — urgent

Update from on-call: pre-warm deployed at 09:50 PT; image registry fallback configured to our US mirror to avoid EU registry lag. Initial telemetry shows p95 back down to ~280–320ms and p99 below ~700ms for FinWare-specific routes. Error rate back to baseline.

We will monitor through the 10 AM peak and keep the pre-warm for 6 hours. Rishi, recommend we keep the autoscaler threshold change in place until next week and open a follow-up to tune scaling by traffic patterns.

Also attaching a heatmap of warmup times and a short excerpt from the container init timeline for the pods that failed fast.

[Attachment: warmup-heatmap-12-01.png]
—Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
SRE (On-call), Redwood Inference
From: evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@finware.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 16:03:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Hosted API: sharp p95/p99 spike this morning — incident summary & next steps

Hi Liam — quick summary and next steps after yesterday's incident. Apologies again for the disruption.

What happened (summary):
- A sudden burst of short-lived sessions triggered aggressive autoscaling in the hosted GPU pool.
- Several newly provisioned nodes experienced extended image-pull times from the EU registry and additional runtime kernel registration overhead, producing cold-start-like first-token delays that manifested as p95/p99 regressions and an uptick in 5xxs.

What we did (immediate mitigations):
- Deployed temporary pre-warm capacity in us-west-2 and switched to a US mirror for image pulls.
- Enabled a warmed, smaller-quantized fallback model for non-critical requests to blunt tail latency.
- Tweaked autoscaler thresholds to reduce simultaneous micro-launches.

Results:
- p95 for your production routes dropped from ~1.2s to ~300ms; p99 is now below 800ms during the monitoring window. Error rate returned to baseline.

Next steps (actions and owners):
- Rishi: pursue registry failover automation + improve image caching for hosted pools (ETA: 2 weeks).
- Jordan: evaluate model cold-start instrumentation and surface an API so customers can request warm pools (ETA: roadmap item Q1).
- Hannah: run a follow-up runbook update and add a canary test that simulates high-volume short-lived sessions (ETA: 5 business days).
- Marissa: coordinate postmortem call and any commercial remediation; proposed 15-minute postmortem today 2:30 PM PT.

Compensation: We recognize impact on FinWare. Marissa will work with you on an appropriate credit. We're also prepared to provide engineering hours for a joint hardening session if you'd like.

I've attached the minute-level p95/p99 CSV and a short debug extract. Please let us know if you'd like the postmortem recording or a deeper dive.

Thanks for your patience,
Evelyn Hart
Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: p95_metrics_20261201.csv]
